extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and policymakers interested in wartime news and occupation policy
extracted.subtask_description: A mid-1940s newspaper page reporting wartime events (Japanese command shakeup, Truk battle), government actions, and summarizing a joint Army-Navy manual on policy for military government in occupied areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary purpose of military government
rubrics_metrics.description: Support of military operations is the primary purpose of military government and achievement of political objectives its secondary purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted from the joint Army-Navy manual: "support of military operations is the primary purpose of military government and achievement of political objectives its secondary purpose." The manual stresses that authority and actions should be directed primarily toward sustaining military operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration/extent of military government
rubrics_metrics.description: Military government may extend beyond active military operations until it achieves the ends of national policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the manual: "As long as military operations continue... some degree of control will be necessary. Military government may extend beyond such operations until it achieves the ends of national policy." This indicates occupation can be prolonged to accomplish political goals tied to national policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to provide substitute civil government
rubrics_metrics.description: Military government has an obligation to provide a substitute for the displaced civil government, including maintenance of order and protection of the local population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual states this obligation explicitly: providing substitutes for displaced civil institutions, maintaining order, and protecting inhabitants are central duties of a military government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of inhabitants must be just and reasonable
rubrics_metrics.description: Just and reasonable treatment of the inhabitants is required, but the degree and nature of that treatment will vary depending principally on the population's attitude toward the occupying forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual emphasizes humane treatment but recognizes practical variation: "Just and reasonable treatment of the inhabitants is required but vary, depending principally on the population’s attitude toward the occupying forces." This frames treatment as both a moral obligation and a pragmatic judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hostages, collective fines, reprisals as last resort
rubrics_metrics.description: Taking hostages, imposing collective fines, and carrying out reprisals may become military necessities but should be regarded as a last resort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual warns against these measures: "such actions are usually an indication of weakness of the occupying forces." They are permissible only when truly necessary and used cautiously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of government offices and legislative bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Some government offices and bureaus may have to be suspended, and legislative bodies usually will be suspended under military government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual notes that legislative bodies 'usually will be suspended' though it allows for practical retention of some offices where feasible; suspension is a common occupational measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of high-ranking political officials; retention of subordinate officials
rubrics_metrics.description: Removal of high-ranking political officials ordinarily is necessary, but subordinate officials and employees of local governments should be retained as far as practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual distinguishes levels of removal: high-ranking figures are typically removed, while subordinate staff should be kept where possible to maintain administration and continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of persons with partisan affiliations
rubrics_metrics.description: Membership in unfriendly partisan organizations or political parties is not necessarily a cause for removal from office, but active leaders will not ordinarily be retained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual advises nuance: mere membership alone does not mandate dismissal, but active leadership in hostile organizations is grounds for non-retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release of persons imprisoned for strictly political reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons imprisoned for strictly political reasons should be released after investigation, with a warning that political activity during the period of military government (may be restricted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual recommends individualized investigation and conditional release rather than blanket continued detention; releases may be accompanied by warnings or restrictions on political activity during occupation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annulment of discriminatory laws
rubrics_metrics.description: Laws which discriminate on the basis of race, color, creed, or political opinions should be annulled as the situation permits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual directs occupying authorities to strike discriminatory legislation when feasible, using the occupation to remove institutionalized discrimination where practical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denaturalization standard re: Falange membership (reported action)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of Justice contends that membership in the Falange (the Spanish Fascist party) is a disqualification to American citizenship and grounds for denaturalization where doctrine is incompatible with the Constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported in the news: the government will assert Falange doctrine is 'incompatible with the well-being of the United States and its Constitution.' The article notes this as the first denaturalization proceeding based on Falange membership and cites the secret oath and Falange aims as evidentiary context.
